fact: WADR reports that access to social media platforms in Guinea was restricted for several days from 28 July 2026 (start date per the ABLOGUI account), with no end date established; the report does not say who ordered it and says it is not the first such restriction.

ABLOGUI says its monitors' tests across Conakry and the regions found a targeted block of Facebook, YouTube and TikTok on 28 July 2026, with no explanation from the ARPT, mobile operators or ISPs; the document names no orderer.

CIPESA says the ECOWAS Court found in the ABLOGUI and others v Guinea case that restrictions on internet and social media access between October and December 2020 violated the applicants' rights to information and freedom of expression.

The Media Foundation for West Africa report, as reported by The Nation, cites the suspension of critical media outlets in Guinea (and Burkina Faso) as a restriction; no outlet, date or law is named, so the document's publication date is used.

Guinea's HAC revoked France 24's national broadcasting authorisation and withdrew its correspondents' press accreditations with immediate effect, citing the channel's refusal to withdraw incriminated remarks, an 'offence' to President Doumbouya.
The HAC ordered the telecoms regulator ARPT to block without delay all France 24 digital access points (websites, streaming feeds, apps) in Guinea, and Canal+ Guinée to cut the channel's signal.

Jeune Afrique reports Facebook, TikTok and YouTube have been inaccessible in Guinea since 28 July 2026, with difficulties on WhatsApp; VPN users get through, which it reads as a deliberate block, and neither the government nor the regulator ARPT has answered; it names no order and gives no end date.
